2026-10-11 · Sky · checked in Australia, United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Germany, New Zealand.

The verdict
Pre-Glued Lash Starter Kit (Lola's Lashes)  Avoid
Demand for pre-glued lash clusters is nearly doubling, but you would be fighting an established brand, 28+ advertisers and cheap Ardell, KISS and GLAM kits in every big chain. Nobody copies Lola's exact kit, yet the category is full.

How to read this

DemandAre more people searching for it than a year ago (last 2 years only), and is Amazon selling units? Green = rising.
Same product in shopsA PHOTO search in each country, then a check of what a shopper finds by typing the product words. Red = in a big chain. Amber = a cheaper copy shoppers will find or trust. Light green = copies exist but are hidden or about the same price. Green = nobody else.
AmazonAre there listings with thousands of reviews? Green = not yet.
AdvertisersHow many brands run Facebook ads for it today, and when did they start? One brand for months = proof. Dozens in the last few weeks = a swarm.
Cost to buyWhat a supplier such as AliExpress charges for it, and what that leaves you per sale. Green = 70% or more left.

Pre-Glued Lash Starter Kit (Lola's Lashes)
Lola's Lashes kit on Amazon UK (£20)

Why avoid

  • Ardell, KISS imPRESS and GLAM pre-glued clusters sit in Target, Walmart, Kmart, Priceline and Chemist Warehouse from about US$12
  • At least 28 brands advertise "pre-glued lashes"; Lola's alone runs 147 of 250 ads and has advertised since February
  • Amazon is heavy: 10,550+ bought last month in the US, and the top listing in Canada has 25,100 reviews

Biggest risk

You would need your own lash brand, safety paperwork and creative good enough to beat established beauty brands on cost per sale.

What to do next

  • Skip this as a product test. If beauty appeals, look for a lash-care add-on (remover, storage, aftercare) with fewer advertisers

Before you order, ask the supplier

  • What is the total cost delivered to my customer's country, per unit?
  • How many days from order to the customer's door?
  • Can you send one sample first, and do you have the safety paperwork this product needs?
